title: Refund Window for the Refund Cover of Northloop Payments Card Settlements
content:
**Rule.** The refund cover of a seller-authorised card settlement of a negative Northloop Payments balance is worked out over a refund window: when the payments account was opened fewer than 365 calendar days before the settlement date, the last month and the last two months are compared and the window whose refund debits are the smaller share of its sale credits is used (the last two months when the shares are equal), so that one unusual week does not set the cover of a young account; when the account was opened at least 1095 (1,095) calendar days before, the window is the last three months; otherwise it is the last month.

A window of the last one, two or three months takes in the ledger entries dated after the same calendar day that many months before the settlement date, up to and including the settlement date. The refund debits and the sale credits of the refund window are both taken over that same window.

## Window by account age

| Calendar days from account opening to the settlement date | Refund window |
|---|---|
| fewer than 365 | the last month or the last two months, whichever has refund debits that are the smaller share of its sale credits; the last two months when the shares are equal |
| 365 to 1094 | the last month |
| 1095 or more | the last three months |

## Hypothetical worked example (account opened 200 days before)

Last month: refund debits 900.00 USD on sale credits 6000.00 USD, a share of 15 percent. Last two months: refund debits 1200.00 USD on sale credits 15000.00 USD, a share of 8 percent. The two-month window has the smaller share, so the refund window is the last two months, with refund debits of 1200.00 USD and sale credits of 15000.00 USD. Had both shares been 8 percent, the last two months would still be used.
